title: New Relic OpenTelemetry Alternatives: 7 OTel Backends
summary: Compare 7 OTel-native New Relic alternatives for engineering teams in 2026. Cut costs, own your data, and discover how Struct complements every stack.
body_markdown:
*Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct*


## Key Takeaways


-


New Relic’s per-seat pricing and NRQL lock-in push teams toward OTel-native backends such as SigNoz, Grafana Cloud, Dash0, and OpenObserve.


-


OTel-native backends accept OTLP natively, so switching providers usually means changing an endpoint instead of re-instrumenting services.


-


Self-hosted options like SigNoz and OpenObserve remove license fees but add operational work, while managed options like Grafana Cloud and Dash0 trade higher usage fees for lower ops overhead.


-


A seven-step dual-write migration playbook with Collector deployment, parity checks, and a controlled cutover lets teams switch backends safely in days to weeks.


-


[Struct adds an automated investigation layer](https://cal.com/deepanm/struct-demo) on top of any backend, turning noisy alerts into fast, verified incident resolution.


## Why Switch from New Relic to OpenTelemetry Alternatives?


Engineering teams switch primarily because of cost and NRQL lock-in.[New Relic’s Pro plan charges $349 per full platform user per month on an annual commitment](https://newrelic.com/pricing) , plus[$0.40 per GB of data ingest beyond the free 100 GB monthly allowance](https://newrelic.com/pricing) . A team of eight engineers pays $2,792 per month in seat fees alone, regardless of how they instrument their applications.


NRQL creates a deeper form of lock-in.[Every dashboard, alert condition, and SLO workflow in New Relic is written in NRQL, which has no equivalent outside the platform](https://cubeapm.com/blog/new-relic-alternatives-with-opentelemetry-support) . Switching instrumentation to OpenTelemetry SDKs keeps that query and alerting layer locked in.[New Relic’s own documentation notes that its proprietary agents work better out of the box than OpenTelemetry SDKs, giving OTel users a second-tier experience on the platform](https://cubeapm.com/blog/new-relic-alternatives-with-opentelemetry-support) .


An “OpenTelemetry-native” backend ingests OTLP as its primary data path and uses the OpenTelemetry data model directly. It does not translate OTLP into a proprietary format after ingestion.[According to Grafana’s 2025 observability survey, 49% of organizations with OpenTelemetry in production cite cost as a key driver for adoption](https://softwareseni.com/vendor-lock-in-escape-and-what-opentelemetrys-otlp-protocol-actually-gives-you) . Once services emit OTLP,[switching backends usually requires changing the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, not re-instrumenting services](https://cubeapm.com/blog/new-relic-alternatives-with-opentelemetry-support) .


## What Are the Best OpenTelemetry Alternatives to New Relic?


The top OTel-native alternatives to New Relic are SigNoz, Grafana Cloud, Dash0, and OpenObserve. The table below compares the four leading OTel-native backends on deployment model and starting price as of September 2026. SigNoz and OpenObserve offer free self-hosted options, while Grafana Cloud and Dash0 are managed SaaS with usage-based fees. Pricing is subject to change and should be verified directly with each vendor before procurement.

The following sections dive deeper into each tool’s pricing, integrations, and limitations so you can weigh trade-offs beyond the headline numbers.


## SigNoz: Open-Source, ClickHouse-Powered, OTel-Native


SigNoz is an open-source APM built natively on OpenTelemetry and ClickHouse, ingesting OTLP with no proprietary agents.[Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34 (April 2026) placed SigNoz at Trial, calling it “a strong self-hosted alternative to platforms such as Datadog.”](https://softwareseni.com/vendor-lock-in-escape-and-what-opentelemetrys-otlp-protocol-actually-gives-you)


**Pricing:**[The Community Edition is free to self-host with no license fee or data caps. Cloud Teams starts at $49/month, which includes $49 of usage credit, then $0.30/GB for logs and traces and $0.10 per million metric samples. Enterprise starts at $4,000/month.](https://cubeapm.com/blog/signoz-pricing-review)


**Best for:** Engineering teams wanting zero vendor lock-in and direct SQL access to raw telemetry in ClickHouse. **Named integrations:** Kubernetes, Docker Compose, Helm charts, Datadog Receiver for incremental migration. **Stated limitation:**[A Reddit user in r/kubernetes noted SigNoz works well only if engineering teams can “wrangle ClickHouse” and give it enough resources](https://cubeapm.com/blog/signoz-pricing-review) . Self-hosting requires real ClickHouse operational expertise.


## Grafana Cloud: The Prometheus-Native Managed Stack


[Grafana Cloud](https://grafana.com/products/cloud/) is a managed observability platform built on the LGTM stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir), accepting OTLP natively. Existing Prometheus metric pipelines and PromQL alert rules carry over without changes.


**Pricing:**[The free tier includes 10,000 active metric series, 50 GB of logs, and 50 GB of traces. Pro starts at a $19/month platform fee plus usage: $6.50 per 1,000 billable metric series, $0.40/GB for log writes, and $8 per active user per month.](https://cloudzero.com/blog/grafana-cloud-pricing)


**Best for:** Engineering teams already invested in Prometheus and PromQL. **Named integrations:** Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Mimir, Grafana Alloy. **Stated limitation:**[Three query languages (PromQL, LogQL, TraceQL) and three storage backends create operational complexity, and many engineering teams find their actual bill lands two to five times higher than their first estimate.](https://cloudzero.com/blog/grafana-cloud-pricing)


## Dash0: Modern, Usage-Based, OTel-First


[Dash0](https://dash0.com/) is an OpenTelemetry-native observability platform with usage-based pricing on data points such as logs, spans, and metric samples rather than hosts, bytes, or seats.[Dash0 acquired Polar Signals](https://dash0.com/) , expanding its continuous profiling capabilities.


**Pricing:**[Pricing is usage-based with no per-user or per-GB charges. Exact starting price is not published on the homepage as of September 2026 and must be confirmed directly with Dash0.](https://dash0.com/)


**Best for:** Engineering teams wanting transparent, predictable pricing and a modern UI. **Named integrations:** Every OTel-compatible tool, agent, or SDK; SignalStore queries via PromQL, SQL, CLI, and API. **Stated limitation:**[Dash0 has a G2 rating of 4.8/5 based on 43 reviews](https://dash0.com/) , which signals a smaller customer base and ecosystem than Grafana or SigNoz and a newer vendor with less community tooling.


## OpenObserve: Lightweight, SQL-Based, Self-Hostable


[OpenObserve](https://openobserve.ai/) is an open-source observability platform written in Rust, unifying logs, metrics, and traces in a single binary backed by object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) and Apache Parquet.[It claims up to 140x lower storage costs than Elasticsearch](https://openobserve.ai/) through columnar compression.


**Pricing:**[The OSS plan is free for self-hosting with no usage limits. The Self Hosted Enterprise plan is free up to 50 GB/day. Cloud plans start with a 14-day free trial; exact subscription pricing is not published on the homepage and requires direct confirmation.](https://openobserve.ai/)


**Best for:** Engineering teams wanting ultra-low storage costs and SQL/PromQL querying without a ClickHouse dependency. **Named integrations:** Native OTel, SQL, PromQL, multi-organization isolation, AI SRE Agent for RCA. **Stated limitation:**[Self-hosting shifts the full operational burden, including scaling, upgrades, and storage management, to your engineering team](https://openobserve.ai/blog/opentelemetry-backends-otlp-support) . The Rust and Parquet architecture also has a steeper learning curve for teams unfamiliar with those technologies.

## How to Migrate from New Relic to OpenTelemetry


A realistic migration for a mid-size engineering team moves through instrumentation replacement, Collector deployment, backend validation, and dashboard rebuild.[Airbnb, Adobe, TRM Labs, and Shopify all independently arrived at dual-write as the only safe migration approach](https://softwareseni.com/enterprise-opentelemetry-migration-playbook-from-proprietary-apm-to-open-standard) . They run both pipelines in parallel before cutting over.


1.


**Instrument your applications with OpenTelemetry SDKs.** Replace New Relic agents with OTel auto-instrumentation.[For mainstream stacks such as Java/Spring, Node.js/Express, and Python/Django, OTel auto-instrumentation now provides comparable coverage to vendor agents](https://intellizu.com/articles/opentelemetry-vs-vendor-agents) , with the gap having narrowed significantly in 2024–2025.


2.


**Set up an OpenTelemetry Collector.** Deploy as a DaemonSet or gateway to receive, process, and export telemetry.[Configure memory_limiter first and batch processor last](https://singhajit.com/opentelemetry-production-guide) . Incorrect processor order causes OOM kills under load.


3.


**Choose and configure your OTel-native backend.** Select from SigNoz, Grafana Cloud, Dash0, or OpenObserve based on your engineering team’s deployment preference and telemetry focus using the decision framework below.


4.


**Export data from the Collector to the new backend.** Update the OTLP exporter endpoint.[Switching backends later becomes a configuration change rather than a re-instrumentation project](https://cubeapm.com/blog/new-relic-alternatives-with-opentelemetry-support) .


5.


**Validate data completeness and parity with New Relic.**[Run dual-write for at least one week. Sample 100 traces per day, verify span counts, and check that latency distribution (P50/P95/P99) matches within 5% and error rates align.](https://tracekit.dev/resources/opentelemetry-migration-guide)


6.


**Decommission New Relic agents and remove NRQL queries.**[Remove vendor SDK imports, agent sidecars, and environment variables such as NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY. Rebuild dashboards and alerts using OTel semantic conventions such as http.request.method instead of http.method.](https://tracekit.dev/resources/opentelemetry-migration-guide)


7.


**Train your engineering team on the new dashboards and alerting.** Document the new query language, whether SQL or PromQL, and alert thresholds.[Use OpenObserve’s AI Assistant or similar tools to bulk-translate NRQL to SQL or PromQL.](https://openobserve.ai/docs/overview/comparison-with-alternatives/newrelic-alternative)


## Self-Hosted vs. Managed: Trade-offs


The core trade-off is operational burden versus control.[With a managed platform, the vendor’s SRE team is paged when ingestion breaks. With a self-hosted stack, the same internal engineers who were supposed to be using the telemetry get paged instead.](https://theclarity.today/story/what-it-really-takes-to-run-opentelemetry-570b0977)


[Self-hosting is labor-dominated in total cost of ownership. A self-hosted stack at roughly 200 hosts costs about $4,900/month, of which approximately $3,000 is engineering time for roughly 20 hours of monthly maintenance.](https://groundcover.com/learn/cost-optimization/observability-platforms-cost-predictability) Self-hosting becomes strategically attractive mainly at 1,000+ hosts or with specific compliance and data-residency requirements.


Managed options such as Grafana Cloud and Dash0 reduce that maintenance burden but introduce usage-based cost curves that grow with telemetry volume.[Self-hosted stacks typically take weeks to months to reach a working production dashboard, whereas managed options reach a working state in hours to days.](https://coralogix.com/guides/self-hosted-vs-managed-observability) For Series A–C engineering teams with 15–80 engineers, the engineering time saved by a managed backend often outweighs the subscription delta until host counts exceed several hundred.


## Decision Framework: Which OTel Alternative Fits Your Team?


Match your engineering team profile to the option that solves your hardest constraint while keeping cost, control, and complexity in balance.


-


**Fully managed, low ops overhead:** Choose Grafana Cloud if already on Prometheus and PromQL. Choose Dash0 if you want usage-based pricing and a modern UI with no per-seat fees.


-


**Self-hosted, open source, zero lock-in:** Choose SigNoz if your engineering team has ClickHouse expertise and wants direct SQL access to raw telemetry. Choose OpenObserve if you want SQL querying, object storage cost savings, and a single-binary deployment.


-


**Regulated industry (fintech, healthtech):**[SigNoz Cloud Teams includes SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance.](https://cubeapm.com/blog/signoz-pricing-review)[Honeycomb Private Cloud, launched January 2026, meets HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and CSA STAR Level 1.](https://softwareseni.com/vendor-lock-in-escape-and-what-opentelemetrys-otlp-protocol-actually-gives-you)


-


**High telemetry volume (>5 TB/month):**[Self-hosted becomes attractive at 1,000+ hosts. Below that threshold, managed is typically cheaper when engineering labor is included in the TCO calculation.](https://groundcover.com/learn/cost-optimization/observability-platforms-cost-predictability)

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are open-source alternatives to New Relic?


SigNoz and OpenObserve are the leading open-source, OTel-native alternatives to New Relic. Both are free to self-host with no license fees. SigNoz is built on ClickHouse and provides a unified APM experience with traces, metrics, and logs. OpenObserve uses Apache Parquet and object storage for significantly lower storage costs. Both accept OTLP natively and require no proprietary agents.


### Why is New Relic so expensive for engineering teams?


New Relic charges $349 per full platform user per month on a Pro annual commitment, plus $0.40 per GB of data ingest beyond the free 100 GB monthly allowance. A team of eight engineers pays $2,792 per month in seat fees regardless of how they instrument their applications. Switching to OpenTelemetry SDKs while staying on New Relic does not reduce this per-seat cost because user pricing is independent of the instrumentation approach.


### How do I migrate from New Relic to OpenTelemetry?


The seven-step process is: replace New Relic agents with OTel SDKs using auto-instrumentation, deploy an OTel Collector with memory_limiter first and batch processor last, choose an OTel-native backend, configure the OTLP exporter endpoint, run dual-write for at least one week to validate parity, decommission New Relic agents and environment variables, then rebuild NRQL dashboards in the new query language such as SQL or PromQL. Engineering teams already using OTel instrumentation can start ingesting into a new backend within hours by updating a single Collector config line.


### Is OpenTelemetry free?


Yes.[OpenTelemetry is a free, open-source CNCF project released under the Apache 2.0 license with no paid tiers, usage limits, or enterprise editions in the project itself.](https://companyview.io/software/opentelemetry)[OpenTelemetry graduated to the highest CNCF maturity tier in May 2026](https://companyview.io/software/opentelemetry) , placing it alongside Kubernetes and Prometheus as a foundational cloud-native standard. The cost appears in the backend you choose. Self-hosted options like SigNoz and OpenObserve are free to run aside from infrastructure and labor, while managed options like Grafana Cloud and Dash0 carry usage-based subscription fees.


### Can Struct work with SigNoz, Grafana, or any OTel-native backend?


Yes. Struct integrates with any observability backend, including SigNoz, Grafana, Datadog, and Sentry. It sits on top as an investigation and incident resolution verification layer and does not replace your observability tooling. When an alert fires, Struct queries your existing backend for logs, metrics, and traces, then correlates those signals with GitHub deploy history and code context. It delivers a root cause hypothesis to Slack, regardless of which backend holds the telemetry.


## Conclusion


New Relic’s per-seat pricing and NRQL lock-in give engineering teams strong reasons to evaluate OTel-native backends. SigNoz and OpenObserve offer zero-license self-hosted paths, while Grafana Cloud and Dash0 provide managed options with lower operational overhead. The migration is manageable with a dual-write approach and a clear seven-step playbook. Switching backends removes cost and lock-in, and adding an automated investigation layer such as Struct addresses the investigation time that follows every alert.
